question.text: A circular coil, carrying a constant current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>i</mi></math> is kept in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>y</mi></math> plane. The magnetic flux through the entire <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>y</mi></math> plane excluding the area of the circular coil is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ϕ</mi></math> and the magnetic flux through the area of the circular coil area is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math>, then

solution.text: As magnetic field lines always form a closed loop, hence every magnetic field line creating magnetic flux in the inner region must be passing through the outer region. So the magnetic flux for one of the regions will be positive and for the other, it will be negative but both will have the same magnitude. This means ϕ=-ϕ0
